page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the n2 family, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM. The processing power is delivered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.8 GHz, featuring 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It has a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show that this instance operates in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1399.29, and the multi-core score is 1841.88. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block transfers measured at 13.72 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.78 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0, reflecting the limited scaling of its dual-thread, single-core architecture.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highcpu-2 is its highly restricted memory capacity of 1.0 GB per core, which limits its utility for modern multi-threaded applications or database hosting. However, it supports advanced CPU instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, CPU-bound tasks that fit within its 2.0 GB memory envelope. Appropriate workloads include basic static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 2.06 GB/sec in testing, simple text processing, and lightweight single-threaded utility scripts.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance includes advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its performance in the lower tiers, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1111.0 and multi-core score of 1311.0, alongside a static web serving throughput of 2.06 GB/sec. Due to its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core, this server is best suited for lightweight, CPU-focused workloads with minimal memory requirements, such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded compilation, or low-traffic static web serving.
